summary: One node in a hand-placed waypoint graph, with per-edge weights that need not be distance.
overview: For open or irregular layouts where a uniform grid does not fit. Edge weight defaults to real distance but can be overridden per edge, so a route can be expensive for reasons that are not physical — danger, difficult terrain, a toll. That override is what makes the graph worth having over a grid.
useCases: A patrol or navigation network through an irregular building.
Routes weighted by danger rather than length.
A small hand-authored graph where baking a navmesh is overkill.

params.tuning: Directed as authored. Two-way travel means adding the edge on both nodes — a very common omission.

gotchas.title: Edges are one-way unless you add both
gotchas.body: A path that works outbound and fails on the return is almost always a missing reverse edge.
